summary: Returns the server's capabilities. Available when the binding's `upload_chunk_size` is greater than zero.

Initializes a new upload resource. The server will respond with a `Location` header containing the specific URL to send data chunks to via PATCH. Available when the binding's `upload_chunk_size` is greater than zero.
Returns the recovery codes for the logged in admin. Recovery codes can be used if the admin loses access to their second factor auth device. Recovery codes are returned unencrypted
Generates new recovery codes for the logged in admin. Generating new recovery codes you automatically invalidate old ones
Returns a list of retention checks that are currently in progress
Returns the recovery codes for the logged in user. Recovery codes can be used if the user loses access to their second factor auth device. Recovery codes are returned unencrypted
Generates new recovery codes for the logged in user. Generating new recovery codes you automatically invalidate old ones
Copies the specified file or directory to the target path for the logged in user. If the target already exists, it will be overwritten
Moves or renames the specified file or directory to the target path for the logged in user
Returns a list of virtual folder quota scans that are currently in progress
Generates a new TOTP secret, including the QR code as png, using the specified configuration for the logged in admin
Checks if the given authentication code can be validated using the specified secret and config name
Returns the cryptographic hash (checksum) of a single file for the logged in user. The operation reads the file content to calculate the hash; for large files, this operation may take some time.
Set supported metadata attributes for the specified file or directory
Returns the available TOTP (Time-based One-Time Password) configurations that the admin can use for two-factor authentication
Returns a list of user quota scans that are currently in progress
Generates a new TOTP secret, including the QR code as png, using the specified configuration for the logged in user
Checks if the given authentication code can be validated using the specified secret and config name

Uploads a single file to the authenticated user's storage by sending the file as the raw request body. Supply the URL-encoded full file path in `path`; an existing file with the same name is overwritten. Use `X-SFTPGO-MTIME` to provide the file modification time in Unix timestamp milliseconds.
Returns the available TOTP (Time-based One-Time Password) configurations that the user can use for two-factor authentication

Saves a TOTP configuration for the authenticated administrator. Set `config_name` to a configuration defined in the `totp` section of the SFTPGo configuration file, and provide a new secret with status `Plain`; status `Redacted` preserves the existing secret. The encryption key and additional data are generated automatically when a new secret is saved.

Saves a TOTP configuration for the authenticated user. Supply a `config_name` defined in the SFTPGo configuration file and select the protocols that require TOTP. Set `secret.status` to `Plain` with a payload to save a new secret, or to `Redacted` to preserve the existing secret.
Manually sets or adjusts the current transfer quota usage (upload and download data) for the given user. Use "reset" mode to set exact values, or "add" mode to increment/decrement the current usage

Retrieves the current byte offset for a resumable user file upload. Use the offset to determine where to resume sending data, and provide the upload ID generated when you created the upload. The response includes the current upload offset.

Uploads a binary chunk to an existing resumable user file upload, or sends the entire file in one chunk. Set `Upload-Offset` to the server's current byte offset and send the chunk as `application/offset+octet-stream`. If the offset conflicts, check the upload status with HEAD and retry from the returned offset.

Updates the used file count and storage size for a virtual folder. Use `mode` to add the supplied values to current usage or reset usage to the supplied values; omitted values default to zero, with different effects depending on the mode.
Creates a new directory within the shared path. The share must have the write scope. Returns 409 if the directory already exists

Starts a new quota scan for the given virtual folder. A quota scan recalculates the number of files and their total size for the specified folder. Returns 409 if a scan is already running for this folder
Disables two-factor authentication for the specified admin. Use this when an admin has lost access to their authenticator device and has no remaining recovery codes

Updates the current disk quota usage for a specified user by setting exact values or adjusting the existing values. Use `mode` to choose between `reset` and `add`; it defaults to `reset` when omitted. Omitted usage values default to 0, with the effect depending on the selected mode.

Starts a new quota scan for the given user. A quota scan recalculates the number of files and their total size for the specified user, including any virtual folders in their quota. Returns 409 if a scan is already running for this user
Disables two-factor authentication for the specified user. Use this when a user has lost access to their authenticator device and has no remaining recovery codes
Returns the log level currently in use by the running application.

Updates the global log level for the running application instance.
**Important:** This setting is **ephemeral** (non-persistent).  The log level will revert to the default configuration (defined in config files or environment variables) upon application restart.
This endpoint is intended for temporary debugging purposes on a live system.

Changes the password for the authenticated user's admin account after verifying the current password. Supply `current_password` for verification and `new_password` as the replacement; the schema specifies no password-format constraints.

Returns provider events (user/admin/folder create, update, delete, etc.) matching the specified filters. Requires the "eventsearcher" plugin to be configured. Supports cursor-based pagination via the from_id parameter
Returns a list of hosts that are currently banned or have recorded violations
Changes the password for the authenticated user. Provide `current_password` so the existing password can be verified, along with the `new_password` to set. The response contains the operation result.

Downloads multiple user files and folders as a ZIP archive streamed without being stored on the server. Send an array of absolute paths in the request body; only regular files and directories are included.
Returns the profile for the currently authenticated admin
Updates the profile for the authenticated user's admin account. Use `email` to set the account email and `allow_api_key_auth` to control whether API keys can be used to impersonate this admin.
Returns the profile for the currently authenticated user

Updates the profile for the authenticated user. Use the body fields to change profile details, API key authentication settings, or public keys; public keys must use OpenSSH authorized_keys format. The response contains the operation result.

Returns log events (login attempts, failed operations, etc.) matching the specified filters. Requires the "eventsearcher" plugin to be configured. Supports cursor-based pagination via the from_id parameter
Invalidates the current user access token before its natural expiration, effectively logging the user out
Returns all sharing links created by the logged in user

Creates a new sharing link for files or folders belonging to the authenticated user. Set `paths` to the shared files or folders and use `scope` to choose read, write, or read/write access; you can also configure restrictions, expiration, and recipient authentication. The share ID is generated automatically and returned in the response headers.
Returns the current usage statistics for your SaaS installation. This endpoint is available only when running SFTPGo as a service
Deletes a file from the authenticated user's storage. Supply the URL-encoded file path in the `path` query parameter to identify the file to remove.
Returns the file contents as the response body. Supports HTTP Range requests for partial downloads
Rename a file for the logged in user. Deprecated, use "file-actions/move"

Uploads one or more files to the authenticated user's storage using `multipart/form-data`. Supply the files in the `filenames` array and use `path` to select a parent directory; omitting `path` targets the root directory. Files with names that already exist are overwritten.
Authenticates a user using HTTP Basic Auth and returns a JWT access token with its expiration. Use this token in the Authorization header as "Bearer <token>" for subsequent user API calls

Returns filesystem events (uploads, downloads, deletes, etc.) matching the specified filters. Requires the "eventsearcher" plugin to be configured. Supports cursor-based pagination via the from_id parameter
Delete a directory and any children it contains for the logged in user
Returns the contents of the specified directory for the logged in user
Rename a directory for the logged in user. The rename is allowed for empty directory or for non empty local directories, with no virtual folders inside
Create a directory for the logged in user. Returns 409 if the directory already exists

Returns the stored configurations of the role that its storage allowlist rejects: the entity, the field the value was read from and the rule that rejected it.
The report is computed on demand. Enabling `resource_isolation` validates the role alone and leaves the stored configurations untouched, so call this endpoint before enabling it to see what the allowlist would reject: narrowing an allowlist applies to the next save of each resource.
The report also carries the posture findings, which describe how wide the isolation is rather than what is wrong with it, and are computed while the role isolates. The report requires the "*" permission: its findings name administrators and resources of every role.

You must set up an SMTP server. SFTPGo will send a code via email to reset the password if the specified admin exists, has a valid email address and is allowed to reset the password. Requests that do not meet these conditions are silently ignored (a success response will be returned) to avoid disclosing existing admins
Resets an administrator's password using a code received by email. Supply the administrator's username, the email code, and the new password to complete the reset.

You must configure an SMTP server. SFTPGo will send a code via email to reset the password if the specified user exists, has a valid email address and does not have the "reset-password-disabled" restriction. Requests that do not meet these conditions are silently ignored (a success response will be returned) to avoid disclosing existing users

Resets a user's password using a code received by email. Submit the code with the new `password` and identify the account with the `username` path parameter. Use the forgot-password operation to request the code before submitting the reset.

Returns the user with the settings inherited from its groups applied, that is the configuration the protocols build at login. A virtual folder mounted on the root path provides the filesystem at login and is reported in `virtual_folders`, the `filesystem` property describes the merge of the user and group configurations. Requires the permissions to view users and groups; the virtual folders are included for administrators that can view folders. For security reasons, the hashed password is omitted from the response
Unbans the specified host and clears all its recorded violations
Returns ban status and violation details for the specified host

Triggers the specified on-demand event rule. The rule's actions will execute asynchronously in the background. To receive a notification when execution completes, add an appropriate action (e.g., email or HTTP callback) to the rule

Returns the file contents as response body. The share must have exactly one path defined and it must point to a directory. Use the path query parameter to specify which file within the shared directory to download
Returns the contents of the specified directory within the share. The share must have exactly one path defined and it must point to a directory
Deletes an existing share belonging to the logged in user
Returns the details of a specific sharing link owned by the logged in user

Updates an existing share belonging to the authenticated user. Pass the share identifier in `id` and provide the share settings to change, including its paths, access scope, or restrictions. Use `[**redacted**]` for `password` to preserve the existing password.

Uploads a single file to a shared path using the raw request body, without multipart encoding. The `filePath` identifies the new file and may include a relative subdirectory; URL-encode special characters in the path. The share must have write scope, and its associated user must have upload or overwrite permission.
Returns the server's capabilities. Available when the binding's `upload_chunk_size` is greater than zero.

Initializes a new upload resource. The server will respond with a `Location` header containing the specific URL to send data chunks to via PATCH. Password-protected shares require HTTP Basic authentication (the share password as the BasicAuth password); the same credentials must be re-sent on every subsequent HEAD and PATCH request for the upload. Available when the binding's `upload_chunk_size` is greater than zero.
Returns a list of event actions. Event actions define what happens when an event rule is triggered (e.g., send email, make HTTP call, execute command)

Creates an event action that can be referenced by event rules. Supply `name` and `type`, then configure the matching sub-object in `options`; sub-objects that do not match `type` are zeroed on save. Use `confidential_data=1` to include confidential values in the response when you have the required permission.
Returns a list of currently active connections, including details about each connected user and their ongoing uploads or downloads
Returns a list of event rules. Event rules define triggers (e.g., file upload, schedule, provider events) and link them to one or more actions

Creates an event rule that connects a trigger and its conditions to an ordered list of actions. Supply `name` and `trigger`, configure exactly one applicable condition in `conditions`, and use `actions` to specify the actions and their execution order.

example.name: notify-on-upload
example.description: Send an email when a file is uploaded

summary: Exports all SFTPGo data (users, folders, admins, etc.) as a provider-independent JSON backup. The backup can either be saved to a file on the server (to avoid exposing sensitive data over the network) or returned directly in the response body. The output can be imported via the loaddata API
Restores SFTPGo data from a JSON backup file stored on the server. Objects are restored one by one; if any object fails to import, the operation stops and a partial restore may result

Restores SFTPGo data and configuration from a JSON backup in the request body. Use `scan-quota` to control quota scanning and `mode` to choose how imported objects affect existing data. Objects are restored one at a time, so a failure can stop the operation after a partial restore.
Returns a list of API keys. For security reasons, hashed keys are omitted from the response. API keys can be used as an alternative to JWT tokens for authentication

Creates a new API key for an administrator or user scope. Set `scope` to `1` for administrator scope or `2` for user scope, and use `admin` or `user` to associate the key with a specific account. A 201 response returns the generated key, so store it securely.

example.mesage: API key created. This is the only time the API key is visible, please save it.

summary: Returns a list of virtual folders. Virtual folders can be mapped into user home directories to provide access to additional storage locations

Creates a new virtual folder with its storage configuration and quota settings. Supply `name` and configure `filesystem` for the storage provider you want to use. Run a quota scan after creation to populate the folder's used file and size counters.
Checks whether the application is running and responding to requests. Returns "ok" if the service is healthy
Returns the current license details including license type, expiration date and enabled features

Sets or updates the license key for the service. Submit the new value in the `key` field; the license takes effect immediately after it is set. Use this operation when you need to replace or apply a license without waiting for a later activation step.
Returns version details including the version number, build date, commit hash and enabled features
Returns a list of admin accounts. For security reasons, hashed passwords are omitted from the response

Creates an administrator account with the supplied account details, permissions, and settings. Use `permissions`, `role`, and `status` to configure access; `status` is `0` for disabled or `1` for enabled. Configure recovery codes and TOTP through their dedicated APIs rather than in this request.
Returns a list of groups. Groups allow you to apply shared settings to multiple users at once, reducing configuration overhead

Creates a new group with its membership, user settings, and virtual folder mappings. Supply `name` to identify the group and include any group settings or associations you want to configure. A 201 response returns the created group.
Invalidates the current admin access token before its natural expiration, effectively logging the admin out
Returns the current status of all active services (SFTP, FTP, WebDAV, HTTP) including their configuration and runtime information
Returns a list of roles. Roles can be assigned to users and admins to control their permissions and scope

Creates a new role that can be assigned to administrators, users, groups, and folders. Supply a unique `name`; set `resource_isolation` to `0` to disable isolation or `1` to enable it, and include `settings` only when the role needs additional settings. The 201 response returns the created role.
Authenticates an admin using HTTP Basic Auth and returns a JWT access token with its expiration. Use this token in the Authorization header as "Bearer <token>" for subsequent API calls
Returns a list of user accounts. For security reasons, hashed passwords are omitted from the response

Creates a new user account with the supplied account, permission, and storage settings. Include `username` and `permissions`; configure `filesystem` for the selected storage provider, and use the dedicated APIs to configure recovery codes or TOTP.

Retrieves the current upload offset for a chunked share upload so you can resume it. Password-protected shares require HTTP Basic authentication using the share password, which is revalidated on every request. Send the required `Tus-Resumable` header with the supported protocol version.

Uploads a chunk of binary data, or the entire file, to an existing share upload. Send the chunk with the required Tus headers, including an `Upload-Offset` that matches the server's current offset. For password-protected shares, authenticate with HTTP Basic using the share password; the password is revalidated on every request.
Deletes an existing event action by its name. Use this operation when you no longer need the action; event rules that reference it may need to be updated.
Returns the event action with the given name if it exists
Replaces the definition of an existing event action. Provide the action's `name` and `type` and the configuration for the matching `options` sub-object; other sub-objects are zeroed on save.
Forcefully terminates an active connection. Any in-progress transfers will be interrupted
Deletes an existing event rule by its name. Use this operation when the rule should no longer trigger its configured actions.
Returns the event rule with the given name if it exists

Replaces the definition of an existing event rule. Provide `name` and `trigger`, configure exactly one applicable condition in `conditions`, and include the actions and ordering you want the rule to use.
Returns the entries in the specified IP list. Use the filter parameter to search for specific IP addresses or networks
Adds an IP address or a CIDR network (e.g., 192.168.1.0/24) to the specified list
Deletes an existing API key. Use the key's `id` to identify which credential to remove. A successful response confirms the operation.
Returns the API key with the given ID if it exists. For security reasons, the hashed key is omitted from the response
Updates an existing API key. The key value, creation date and last use timestamp cannot be changed

Deletes an existing folder. The folder must not be referenced by any user or group; detach it from every referencing user and group first. Mirrors the symmetric guard on `DELETE /api/v2/groups/{name}`.
Returns the virtual folder with the given name if it exists

Updates the configuration of an existing virtual folder. Identify the folder with `name` and provide its configuration in the request body. Use `filesystem.provider` to select the active storage configuration; unused provider configurations are ignored or cleared when saved.
Deletes an existing administrator account identified by its username. Use this operation when you need to remove an administrator; the `username` must identify the account to delete.
Returns the admin with the given username if it exists. For security reasons, the hashed password is omitted from the response

Updates an existing administrator account identified by its username. Use this operation to change administrator details and settings, but use the dedicated APIs for recovery codes and TOTP configuration; you cannot update the administrator impersonated by an API key.
Deletes an existing group. The group must not be referenced by any user or administrator; detach it from every referencing account first.
Returns the group with the given name if it exists

Replaces the configuration of an existing group. Supply the required `name` and any group settings you want to set, including associated users, administrators, permissions, or virtual folders. The `created_at`, `id`, and `updated_at` fields are read-only and are not writable group settings.

Downloads a ZIP archive containing the files and directories in a share. The share must have read scope, and its associated user must have list and download permissions; only regular files and directories are included. Set `compress` to control compression, or omit it to use the default of `true`.

Uploads one or more files to a shared path using `multipart/form-data`. The share must have write scope, and its associated user must have upload permission. Include files in the `filenames` array; each file must be unique and the array must contain at least one item.
Deletes an existing role. The role must not be referenced by any administrator or user; clear the role from every referencing account first.

Retrieves the role with the specified name. Use this operation to inspect a role's description, resource isolation level, settings, and associated administrators and users. The response includes the role's creation and update timestamps.

Replaces the configuration of an existing role. Supply the required `name` and the role settings to apply; `resource_isolation` accepts `0` or `1`, and `settings` can hold additional role configuration. The `admins` and `users` fields are set on read and are not writable role settings.
Deletes an existing user account identified by its username. Use this operation when you need to remove a user; the `username` must identify the account to delete.
Returns the user with the given username if it exists. For security reasons, the hashed password is omitted from the response

Updates an existing user's account settings and can disconnect the user after a successful update. Supply the user's configuration in the request body; omitting the password preserves the current password, and recovery codes and TOTP settings must be managed through their dedicated APIs. Set `disconnect` to 1 to require the user to log in again and apply the updated settings.

Deletes an existing entry from an IP list. Use `type` to select the list and `ipornet` to identify the address or network entry to remove. The list type must be one of the supported values: allow list, defender, rate limiter safe list, or trusted list.
Retrieves an IP list entry by its type and IP address or network. Use `type` to select the list and `ipornet` to identify the entry; IP addresses and networks use CIDR notation.

Replaces the values of an existing IP list entry. Supply the entry's `type` and `ipornet` in the path, then provide the entry values to update in the request body. The body can include the entry's mode, protocols, and description.
